title: Man dead in police shooting
subtitle: A Scott Street resident described by a neighbour as "special needs" died Tuesday night after being shot by a Midland police officer.
article: A Scott Street resident described by a neighbour as "special needs" died Tuesday night after being shot by a Midland police officer.
Douglas Heagle, 38, was pronounced dead at Huronia District Hospital.
The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) is looking into the incident, which took place at 238 Scott St. shortly after 5 p.m.

"Midland police advised the SIU that just before 5 p.m., two officers responded to a 911 call, at which time they interacted with a man outside the home," SIU spokesperson Frank Phillips stated in a news release. "An officer fired at least one shot and the man was struck."
The original nature of the call, Phillips told The Mirror, will not be released.
"That's between Midland police and the 911 caller," he said, adding the SIU is looking at what transpired between the victim and the police officers.

"We've identified four officers that actually went to the call," he said. "As to how long they were on the scene, that's something that will form part of our investigation, which is ongoing at this point."
The SIU has designated one officer as the subject officer and the other three as witness officers.
Investigators were on the scene Wednesday morning, he said, noting they've learned three of the responding officers entered the house when they arrived on the scene.
"Two of them came out with the gentleman," said Phillips, "and (the shooting) happened in the driveway outside."
Kip Papke, who lives across the street, was home when the shooting took place. He told The Mirror he is stunned by what happened.

"When my wife first looked out the window, we saw Doug on the ground by the side door with two officers standing over him," he said, adding he did not hear a gunshot. "We thought maybe he'd had a seizure or slipped and fell."
Papke described Heagle as the adopted special-needs son of the homeowner.

"He's a bit slow and his speech is impaired a little," he said, adding the mother is reportedly staying with neighbours. "I talked to her briefly last night.... She seemed a little distraught.... She's not well."
Papke said while he has spoken to Heagle in the past, he doesn't know him well.
This isn't the first time police have been called to the home, he added: "I have seen the cops there a couple of times."
Nonetheless, Papke said it's a shock a man was shot in what he described as a quiet neighbourhood.
This is the first time in more than 20 years an officer with the Midland Police Service has had to use a firearm on a person, according to Chief Paul Hamelin.

"We have never caused injury to a person with a firearm in my history here," Hamelin told The Mirror last week. "Sometimes, an officer will have to use their firearm to put (an) animal out of its suffering ... but I can't recall a time when we've had to discharge our firearms at a person.
"Our officers are very good and diligent at, through tactical communication, gaining compliance with the folks we're dealing with and convincing them to do what we need them to do."
Police departments are guided by a "use-of-force continuum" designed by the province and the Ontario Police College. It includes a variety of options, including tactical communication.

"When you arrest someone, you have to take physical control of them," said Hamelin, adding other options include physical techniques such as escorting holds, defensive moves and stronger hand techniques such as having to strike somebody using a restraining hold.
Next are more severe applications of force such as pepper spray, batons, Tasers and firearms.

"With all that equipment on your belt, you have to decide which is the most appropriate application of force you're going use," said Hamelin. "Our whole purpose is to use the least amount of force possible to gain compliance with whatever process going through."
The SIU has assigned four investigators and two forensic investigators to probe the incident. A post-mortem is expected to take place this morning (Feb. 5).
